explanation: The scheduler is work-conserving: when UDP demand is below its configured share, TCP can use the unused UDP share, so TCP goodput is not simply capped by 1 - weightUdp (E1, C1, V1). UDP is offered at about 300 Mbps payload. With queuePkts=100 and TcpCubic, UDP loss becomes unacceptable below the measured boundary: weightUdp=0.3030 gives udp_loss_frac=0.011151, while weightUdp=0.3036 gives udp_loss_frac=0.009736, just below the 1% limit (E3, C7, V7). Because the link is saturated and total delivered payload is nearly constant (E2, C6, V6), TCP goodput is maximized by choosing the smallest configured UDP share that still satisfies the UDP-loss constraint. weightUdp=0.3036 is the lowest tested feasible weight and gives tcp_goodput_bps=671509421 at seed 1; it remains feasible for seeds 1-8, with udp_loss_frac between 0.009733 and 0.009736 and TCP goodput around 671.5 Mbps (E4, E5, C15). queuePkts=100 is the best tested queue size: queuePkts=4, 20, 50, and 200 do not improve TCP goodput materially, while queuePkts=1000 reduces TCP goodput and queuePkts=4 causes many TCP drops (E2, C3, V3, E3, C8, V8). TcpCubic is recommended because it fills the link; TcpBbr and TcpVegas materially underutilize it, and TcpLinuxReno, TcpNewReno, and TcpBic are not materially better than TcpCubic in the tested region (E2, C4, V4, E3, C9, V9). Seed and duration are not meaningful performance levers in the tested range; seed=1 and duration=10 are recommended for reproducibility, and any seed among 1-8 should give essentially the same result.
holds_when: The fixed system remains a single 1 Gbps link with 50 us one-way delay, 1500-byte MTU, a constant 300 Mbps UDP application sending 1400-byte packets, a greedy TCP sender, a work-conserving scheduler with separate UDP and TCP queues, and a measured steady-state window. The recommendation is supported for TcpCubic, queuePkts around 100, and seeds 1-8 tested here.
breaks_when: It would change if the UDP offered load changes, if the scheduler is not work-conserving, if the UDP-loss constraint is stricter than 1%, if queuePkts is made very large or very small, if a different TCP variant is required, if seeds beyond those tested shift the UDP-loss boundary, or if duration effects alter the measured steady-state average. A weight slightly below 0.3036 might be feasible if the exact boundary lies between 0.3030 and 0.3036, but it was not tested.

claims.text: The scheduler is work-conserving: TCP can use UDP capacity that UDP does not demand.
UDP loss appears when the configured UDP share is below the UDP demand share; with queuePkts=100 and TcpCubic the 1% UDP-loss boundary is between weightUdp=0.3030 and 0.3036.
At weightUdp=0.3036, queuePkts=100, TcpCubic, seed=1, udp_loss_frac=0.009736 <= 0.01 and tcp_goodput_bps=671509421.
In the saturated region, total delivered UDP plus TCP payload is nearly constant, so reducing the configured UDP share while keeping UDP loss <= 1% increases TCP goodput.

queuePkts=100 is preferable to very small or very large queues: larger queues do not materially reduce UDP loss and reduce TCP goodput, while very small queues cause TCP drops without improving TCP goodput.
TcpCubic is among the best TCP variants for this goal; TcpBbr and TcpVegas underutilize the link, and TcpLinuxReno, TcpNewReno, and TcpBic are not materially better than TcpCubic.
The recommended weightUdp=0.3036 is robust across seeds 1-8: udp_loss_frac remains <= 0.01 and TCP goodput remains about 671.5 Mbps.
weightUdp=0.304 is a robust fallback with udp_loss_frac=0.007888 across seeds 1-5 and tcp_goodput_bps about 670.96 Mbps.

open_questions: The exact 1% UDP-loss boundary between weightUdp=0.3030 and 0.3036 was not located; a value such as 0.3035 might be feasible.
The effect of duration values other than the default 10 seconds was not tested.
Seeds beyond 1-8 were not tested, although seed variation was very small in the tested range.
Whether TcpBic or another variant could give a tiny TCP gain at exactly weightUdp=0.3036 was not tested.
Whether queuePkts=200 or another moderate queue size could reduce TCP drops at weightUdp=0.3036 without changing goodput was not directly tested.
